events.summary: Worcester 20s & 30s November Social at NU Kitchen

description.plain:
Thursday, November 13, 2025 | 6:00 PM
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UUN000001uEfd2AE/
Join us for a social at NU Kitchen in Worcester on Thursday, November 13th at 6:00pm! Hang out with other young members and leaders from the Worcester Chapter and learn about fun upcoming trips this winter. Everyone is welcome-- new and returning participants! NU Kitchen offers a variety of salads, grain bowls, sandwiches, smoothies, and breakfast foods. Hope to see you there!Registration is required so the leader can be in touch in case of change of venue.

Warner, NH

description.plain:
Saturday, November 22, 2025
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UUN000001tTTp2AM/
Join the Worcester 20s & 30s group for a hike of Mt. Kearsarge (South) in Warner, NH on Saturday, November 22nd! This hike will be just under 10 miles and around 2,500 ft elevation gain. Our intention is to go at a roughly a 1.5 mile per hour pace. Expect to be on trail for the full day.Mt. Kearsarge is part of NH's 52 with-a-view list. On a clear day, you can see the Boston skyline as well as a 360-degree view!Sturdy shoes with laces, at least 2 liters of water, snacks/lunch, and appropriate layers of clothing are required. Participants should be prepared for winter conditions and will likely be requested to bring microspikes in case of ice at higher elevations. No dogs, please. Further details, such as start time and location, will be provided to participants after they complete the required screening form, which will be sent after registering. Hope to have you join us!

Sunday, November 30, 2025
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UUN000001vqpP2AQ/
Let’s bid a fond farewell to fall with one final hike! Climb to the summit of Mt. Wataticwith us to take in spectacular views from its open peak that stretch from Mount Greylockin the west to Boston in the east. Ascend on old cart roads through stands of red mapleand white wood asters and then descend back down the rocky western slope to see..abig rock!This 2.8 mile loop with 700’ of elevation gain is expected to take 2-3 hours. It’s a veryapproachable trip for novice hikers with good mobility and those who identify asphysically active. We’ll plan to keep a moderate pace (1.5mph) to ensure we staytogether as a group. This is a popular hike, so you can expect a well-trodden dirt pathon the ascent. The descent from Mount Watatic is rocky and uneven, so you mayappreciate bringing a set of hiking poles.Daytime highs in Ashburnham and Ashby have been ranging from just below freezing(32F) to 50F lately, so make sure you’re come dressed in layers and prepared for coldweather. Puffy jackets or a similar insulating layer are a must, as well as a hat and set ofgloves/mittens. Mount Watatic’s peak is exposed, so pack a wind-proof outer layer toward off the chill. Trip leaders will be monitoring the weather for icy conditions inadvance since light rain and freeze/thaw conditions are expected in the next coupleweeks.You can expect an email with further details, including the exact meeting time, one weekin advance of the trip.Any cancellations due to weather will be sent out via email the day before the trip.Rain, stormy weather, or icy conditions will cancel this trip.
